```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

## Model

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Adult SES}_i &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma) \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \beta\,\text{Family SES}_i
\end{aligned}
$$

- Family: Normal.
- Linear model: intercept $\alpha$, slope $\beta$.
- Parameters needing priors: $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\sigma$.

## Standardized variables

```{r}
#| label: standardize

mobility <- read_mobility()
mean_sd_table(mobility, w1_ses, w4_ses, parent_ses_z, adult_ses_z)
```

- n = `r format(nrow(mobility), big.mark = ",")` students with both SES
  measures.
- `parent_ses_z` (family SES, 2002) and `adult_ses_z` (adult SES, 2012):
  mean 0, SD 1.

## Intercept

```{r}
#| label: fig-intercept-priors
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3

intercept_priors <- c(prior_normal(0, 0.2), prior_normal(0, 0.5), prior_normal(0, 1))

plot_priors(intercept_priors, x_label = "α, expected adult SES at family SES = 0 (SD)", limits = c(-3, 3))
```

- 95% of each prior:
  - Normal(0, 0.2): `r interval_text(intercept_priors[[1]])`.
  - Normal(0, 0.5): `r interval_text(intercept_priors[[2]])`.
  - Normal(0, 1): `r interval_text(intercept_priors[[3]])`.

## Slope

```{r}
#| label: fig-slope-priors
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3

slope_priors <- c(prior_normal(0, 0.5), prior_normal(0, 1))

plot_priors(
  slope_priors,
  x_label = "β, expected difference in adult SES per SD of family SES",
  limits = c(-3, 3), possible = c(-1, 1)
)
```

- Possible values: −1 to 1. With both variables standardized, the slope is
  the correlation.
- Normal(0, 0.5): 95% `r interval_text(slope_priors[[1]])`; share between
  −1 and 1: `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_share(slope_priors[[1]], -1, 1))`.
- Normal(0, 1): 95% `r interval_text(slope_priors[[2]])`; share between
  −1 and 1: `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_share(slope_priors[[2]], -1, 1))`.

## Residual SD

```{r}
#| label: fig-sigma-priors
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3

sigma_priors <- c(prior_exponential(1), prior_half_normal(1), prior_half_t(3, 2.5))

plot_priors(
  sigma_priors,
  x_label = "σ, SD of adult SES around the line (SD)",
  limits = c(0, 4), possible = c(0, 1)
)
```

- Possible values: greater than 0 and at most 1, the SD of adult SES.
- Exponential(1): mean 1. 95% `r interval_text(sigma_priors[[1]])`; share
  above 1: `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_share(sigma_priors[[1]], 1, Inf))`.
- Half-normal(0, 1): Stan prior recommendations. 95%
  `r interval_text(sigma_priors[[2]])`; share above 1:
  `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_share(sigma_priors[[2]], 1, Inf))`.
- Half-t(3, 0, 2.5): brms default, `student_t(3, 0, 2.5)` with a lower bound
  of 0. 95% `r interval_text(sigma_priors[[3]])`; share above 1:
  `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_share(sigma_priors[[3]], 1, Inf))`.

## Prior predictive simulation

### Prior sets

```{r}
#| label: prior-sets

prior_sets <- list(
  Weaker = prior_set(alpha = prior_normal(0, 1), beta = prior_normal(0, 1), sigma = prior_half_t(3, 2.5)),
  Stronger = prior_set(alpha = prior_normal(0, 0.2), beta = prior_normal(0, 0.5), sigma = prior_exponential(1))
)
mu <- ~ alpha + beta * parent_ses_z

prior_set_table(prior_sets)
```

- Weaker: the widest candidate for each parameter above; its residual SD
  prior is the brms default.

### Implied lines

```{r}
#| label: fig-prior-lines
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5

draws <- draw_priors(prior_sets, n = 4000)

plot_prior_lines(draws, mu, x_label = "Family SES (SD)", y_label = "Expected adult SES (SD)")
```

### Simulated data

```{r}
#| label: fig-simulated
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

students <- slice_sample(mobility, n = 200) |> select(parent_ses_z)
simulated <- simulate_outcomes(draws, students, mu)

plot_simulated(simulated, parent_ses_z, x_label = "Family SES (SD)", y_label = "Simulated adult SES (SD)")
```

- Family SES: real values for 200 students. Adult SES: simulated.

### Implied outcome SD

```{r}
#| label: fig-outcome-sd
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4

stats <- simulated_stats(simulated, outcome_sd = sd(y))
plot_simulated_stats(stats, reference = c(outcome_sd = 1), log_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: outcome-sd-summary

outcome_sd_summary <- stats |>
  summarise(median = median(outcome_sd), share_above_2 = mean(outcome_sd > 2), .by = set)
outcome_sd_summary |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

- Outcome SD: the SD of simulated adult SES in each simulated data set.
- Observed: adult SES is standardized with the sample's SD, so any data set
  on this scale has an SD near 1.
